subject: Re: SLA commitments — request for termination rights & fee-at-risk
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@finova.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finova.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA commitments — termination rights & fee-at-risk

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement counsel reviewed the SaaS terms and they flagged the standard credits-only approach for downtime. For Finova to sign, legal is asking for one of the following:

- explicit termination rights if Redwood misses the Monthly Uptime SLO for two consecutive months; OR
- a fee-at-risk / liquidated-damages schedule (we proposed 5% of monthly committed fees for the first material breach, escalating thereafter).

We appreciate credits are common, but the bank needs a stronger economic remedy tied to availability for this regulated environment. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept termination rights or a fee-at-risk schedule?

Also attaching our suggested redline of the SLA for your review (Finova_Redline_SLA_v3.docx).

Best,
Elena Suarez
Director, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Finova Capital

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@finova.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA commitments — termination rights & fee-at-risk

Elena —

Thanks for sending the redline and context. I understand Finova's position and the need for stronger remedies in a regulated environment. Quick note up-front: Redwood's standard public contract offers service credits for SLO misses and limited termination for prolonged systemic failure, but we have flexibility for enterprise deals.

I’m looping in Rishi (account lead) and Laura (legal) to evaluate the proposed language. We should be able to propose a path that balances predictable remedies with protections for both parties (e.g., a calibrated fee-at-risk for repeat, substantiated outages, or termination tied to a clear set of objective breaches).

Would you be open to a short call this week so we can walk through the redline line-by-line? I can bring our legal counsel and Head of Reliability.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.coale@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0113

Attachment: Finova_Redline_SLA_v3.docx (see highlighted termination / remedies section)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA commitments — termination rights & fee-at-risk (Finova)

Team — forwarding Finova’s ask. Key points to consider:

1) Business: Finova is target ACV $425k ARR first-year committed. They’re in regulated finance; procurement escalated.
2) Risk: Customer proposes termination after two consecutive months below Monthly Uptime SLO or fee-at-risk starting 5%. That’s more aggressive than our template.
3) Options I think we can offer without exposure to open-ended liability:
   - Compromise A: Replace termination-for-two-months with termination after three consecutive months documented and unremediated AND a remediation plan attempt (gives us runway).
   - Compromise B: Fee-at-risk capped at 10% of 3-month committed fees annually, with credits offsetting fees (so we avoid double recovery). Initial fee at 3% first material breach, 5% on second within 12 months.
   - Compromise C: No fee-at-risk; expanded credits + guaranteed onboarding/ops playbook + quarterly ops review + an SLA escrow for logs during incidents.

4) Commercial mitigation: add service credits up front (e.g., 25% credit for full-month <=99.0% availability; 50% if <=97.5%), plus the escalation language above.

Laura — can you run legal on the above and weigh in on preferred language (especially the caps and offset)? Markus — want your opinion on whether we can accept a three-month termination trigger from reliability/ops perspective.

-Rishi

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: SLA commitments — termination rights & fee-at-risk (Finova)

Thanks — I reviewed Finova_Redline_SLA_v3.docx and put comments on the termination and remedies section. High-level legal position:

- We should avoid unconditional termination based solely on two calendar months of underperformance. We can accept termination tied to repeated, documented, unremedied breaches with an opportunity to cure (suggest 60 days) and objective measurement (mutually agreed monitoring/reporting).
- Fee-at-risk / liquidated damages: acceptable if narrowly scoped, capped, and subject to offset by credits. Proposed legal language: fees at risk capped at a fixed percentage of the monthly committed fees (e.g., 3–5%), and an aggregate annual cap (e.g., 10% of annual committed fees). Include explicit offset for any credits paid.
- We should also require that customer exhausts the operational remedies (e.g., activate our incident response playbook, joint post-incident review) before termination/right to claim damages.

I will produce a redline that implements: termination after 3 sequential Monthly SLO misses with 60-day cure, a tiered fee-at-risk (3% first / 5% second breach in 12 months) with an annual cap at 10% and mandatory credit offset. I’ll also add measurable metric definitions and reporting cadence.

Will send the redline by EOD. Laura

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@finova.com>, ops@finova.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SLA commitments — termination rights & fee-at-risk

Elena — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this with legal and reliability. Summary of our proposed approach (attached redline and appendix):

1) Termination: we can agree to a termination right tied to repeated, objective breaches — specifically: three (3) consecutive Monthly Uptime SLO misses for which Redwood failed to (a) implement the mutually agreed remediation plan and (b) cure within 60 days after written notice. This replaces the two-month termination Finova proposed.

2) Fee-at-risk / liquidated damages: we’ll accept a narrow, tiered fee-at-risk structure: 3% of the monthly committed fees for the first material breach within a 12-month rolling window, increasing to 5% for a second breach within the same 12 months. All fee-at-risk amounts are offset dollar-for-dollar by any service credits already paid for the same incident(s). Aggregate annual cap of 10% of total committed fees.

3) Operational guardrails: before termination or fee-at-risk applies, Finova must engage the joint incident response playbook and participate in a post-incident review. Metrics and monitoring sources must be mutually agreed and attached as an Appendix (see SLA_Metrics_Appendix.xlsx).

4) Next steps: Laura attached a redline implementing the above (Finova_SLA_Redline_from_Redwood_v1.docx). If that captures Finova’s intent, can we schedule a 30-min contract call Thursday to confirm language and get to an approval path? We’re prepared to present this with a short examples table showing how credits and fee offsets would calculate across typical outage scenarios.

We want to be reasonable and predictable — protect Finova from repeated failures while keeping liability capped and operationally driven. Happy to jump on a call with your counsel.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.coale@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0113

Attachments: Finova_SLA_Redline_from_Redwood_v1.docx; SLA_Metrics_Appendix.xlsx
